dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A local definition taking a type Ω with a measurable-space structure, a measure μ on Ω, and a function X : Ω → ℝ, returning the real number `MeasureTheory.integral μ (fun ω => X ω)`, i.e. the Bochner integral ∫ X dμ. Since μ is a probability measure in the target, this is the expectation E[X].
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies both sides of the inequality: φ(∫ X dμ) on the left and ∫ (φ ∘ X) dμ on the right. Under the probability-measure hypothesis it is exactly the expectation operator, so the target reads φ(E X) ≤ E[φ(X)]. Note it is defined via the Bochner integral, which returns 0 for non-integrable functions — hence the integrability hypotheses matter.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.id
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical algebra structure of a commutative semiring R over itself, with algebra map the identity ring homomorphism and scalar multiplication given by ring multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Purely instance plumbing: it makes ℝ an ℝ-algebra so that the scalar action ℝ ↷ ℝ used by ConvexOn is ordinary real multiplication. No new mathematical content; it fixes the meaning of a•x as a*x.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection extracting the scalar-multiplication (SMul R A) field from an Algebra R A structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing: combined with Algebra.id it yields the SMul ℝ ℝ instances used in both slots of ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ, so convex combinations are a*x + b*y with ordinary real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: CommSemiring.toSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection from a commutative semiring structure to its underlying semiring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing only; supplies the Semiring ℝ argument needed to form Algebra.id-derived SMul instances. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: ConvexOn
dependency_coverage.meaning: ConvexOn 𝕜 s f is the conjunction of (i) Convex 𝕜 s, i.e. s is a convex set, and (ii) for all x, y ∈ s and all scalars a, b with 0 ≤ a, 0 ≤ b, a + b = 1, one has f(a•x + b•y) ≤ a•f(x) + b•f(y).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the hypothesis hφ: φ : ℝ → ℝ is convex on the whole real line (s = Set.univ, which is trivially convex), i.e. midpoint/convex-combination inequality holds for all pairs of reals. This is the substantive analytic hypothesis driving Jensen's inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The generic `≤` relation projected out of an LE α instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the order relation in the conclusion, instantiated at ℝ with Real.instLE, so the conclusion is the ordinary ≤ on real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The structure of a σ-algebra on a type: a collection of measurable sets closed under complement and countable union, containing the empty set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Equips Ω with a σ-algebra so that measures and integrals over Ω are meaningful. It is an instance binder in the statement; no restriction beyond existence of some σ-algebra.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Integrable
dependency_coverage.meaning: Integrable f μ means f is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ AND has finite integral (∫⁻ ‖f‖ dμ < ∞).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides hypotheses hX (X is μ-integrable) and hφX (φ ∘ X is μ-integrable). These guarantee both Bochner integrals in the conclusion are genuine finite integrals rather than the junk value 0 the Bochner integral assigns to non-integrable functions.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A typeclass asserting that the measure of the whole space is 1, i.e. μ(univ) = 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes μ a probability measure, so ∫ · dμ is expectation, X is a real random variable, and the convex-combination argument (total mass 1) is available. Without it the inequality would be false in general.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of (countably additive, [0,∞]-valued) measures on a measurable space, built on an outer measure with measurability of all measurable sets and countable additivity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The type of μ, the measure with respect to which both integrals are taken.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalSeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Structure projection from a non-unital seminormed commutative ring to its non-unital seminormed ring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing in the derivation of the norm/ENorm structure on ℝ used by Integrable. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalSeminormedRing.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Derives a seminormed additive commutative group structure from a non-unital seminormed ring, reusing its norm, additive group, and pseudometric.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing: part of the chain producing the ContinuousENorm ℝ argument of Integrable. Fixes the norm on ℝ as the usual absolute value. No mathematical content beyond that.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedCommRing.toSeminormedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Structure projection weakening a normed commutative ring to a seminormed commutative ring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing in the same chain fixing ℝ's norm for the Integrable hypotheses. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection extracting the uniform-space structure canonically attached to a pseudometric space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing supplying the topology on ℝ used by Integrable (via UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace). Fixes the standard topology of ℝ.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers (Cauchy-completion of ℚ).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The codomain of the random variable X, the domain and codomain of φ, the scalar field for convexity, and the type of both sides of the concluding inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive commutative monoid instance on ℝ (ordinary addition with 0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the AddCommMonoid arguments (for both E = ℝ and β = ℝ) of ConvexOn, so the additions in a•x + b•y and a•φ(x) + b•φ(y) are ordinary real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instCommSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: The commutative semiring instance on ℝ (usual addition and multiplication).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing feeding Algebra.id / Algebra.toSMul so the ℝ-scalar action on ℝ is real multiplication in the ConvexOn hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical ≤ ordering on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The order used in the conclusion φ(∫X dμ) ≤ ∫ φ(X) dμ; it is the standard real ordering, not some exotic order.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normed commutative ring structure on ℝ with norm the absolute value and the usual metric d(x,y)=|x−y|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Root of the instance chain giving the ContinuousENorm ℝ needed by Integrable; ensures 'integrable' means the standard finiteness of ∫|X| dμ.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.partialOrder
dependency_coverage.meaning: The partial order structure on ℝ (which is in fact a total order), built from Real.instLE and Real.instLT with reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the PartialOrder 𝕜 = ℝ and PartialOrder β = ℝ arguments of ConvexOn, so the constraints 0 ≤ a, 0 ≤ b and the convexity inequality use the standard real order.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.pseudoMetricSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The pseudometric space structure on ℝ with dist x y = |x − y|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing giving ℝ its standard uniformity/topology for the Integrable hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.semiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: The semiring instance on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the Semiring 𝕜 = ℝ argument of ConvexOn, fixing ℝ as the scalar semiring for convex combinations.

dependency_coverage.name: SeminormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets commutativity, producing a seminormed additive group from a seminormed additive commutative group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing in the chain producing ContinuousENorm ℝ for Integrable. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: SeminormedAddGroup.toContinuousENorm
dependency_coverage.meaning: Builds a continuous extended-norm (ENorm with continuity) structure from a seminormed additive group, using the coercion of the nonnegative norm into ℝ≥0∞.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the ContinuousENorm ℝ argument that Integrable requires; ensures 'finite integral' is measured by the usual |·| on ℝ.

dependency_coverage.name: SeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets the unit, producing a non-unital seminormed commutative ring from a seminormed commutative ring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing in the ℝ-norm chain for Integrable. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: The universal set {a | True} of a type, containing every element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The domain of convexity: φ is assumed convex on all of ℝ, not merely on a subinterval. This is a strengthening of the hypothesis relative to convexity on a proper convex subset, and it removes any need for a hypothesis that X takes values in a specified set.

dependency_coverage.name: UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection giving the topology induced by a uniform structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instance plumbing supplying TopologicalSpace ℝ to Integrable. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection from an inner product space structure to its underlying normed space structure over the same scalar field.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Distance-2 instance plumbing used to obtain NormedSpace ℝ ℝ for the Bochner integral inside LocalDef001. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.integral
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Bochner integral ∫ a, f a ∂μ of a function f : α → G into a real normed space G with respect to a measure μ; it is defined to be 0 when f is not integrable (or the space is not complete/measurable in the required sense).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The actual operator underlying LocalDef001, so both sides of the conclusion are Bochner integrals over μ. Its junk-value convention on non-integrable functions is exactly why the two Integrable hypotheses are needed for the statement to be meaningful.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Weakens a normed additive commutative group to a seminormed one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Distance-2 instance plumbing for the ℝ norm structures used by the integral and integrability predicates. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an RCLike field 𝕜 (i.e. ℝ or ℂ), the canonical real inner product space structure on 𝕜.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Distance-2 instance plumbing that ultimately gives NormedSpace ℝ ℝ for the Bochner integral over ℝ-valued functions. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instRCLike
dependency_coverage.meaning: The instance exhibiting ℝ as an RCLike field (a complete densely normed field with trivial imaginary part, re = id, im = 0, I = 0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Distance-2 instance plumbing in the chain giving ℝ its NormedSpace ℝ ℝ structure for the integral. No mathematical content.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normed additive commutative group structure on ℝ with norm the absolute value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Distance-2 instance supplying the NormedAddCommGroup ℝ argument of MeasureTheory.integral, fixing the target space of the Bochner integral as ℝ with its usual norm.

binders: Ω : Type (implicit, arbitrary universe u_1) — the sample space
[inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] — an instance binder equipping Ω with a σ-algebra
μ : Measure Ω (implicit) — a measure on Ω
[IsProbabilityMeasure μ] — an instance binder asserting μ(Ω) = 1
X : Ω → ℝ (implicit) — a real-valued function (random variable) on Ω
φ : ℝ → ℝ (implicit) — a real-valued function on the reals
hφ : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ — named hypothesis of convexity
hX : Integrable X μ — named hypothesis
hφX : Integrable (fun ω => φ (X ω)) μ — named hypothesis
hypotheses: μ is a probability measure on the measurable space (Ω, inst): μ(Ω) = 1.
φ is convex on the whole real line: Set.univ ⊆ ℝ is convex (trivially), and for all x, y ∈ ℝ and all real a, b with a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, a + b = 1, one has φ(a·x + b·y) ≤ a·φ(x) + b·φ(y).
X is μ-integrable: X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ and ∫⁻ ‖X‖ dμ < ∞.
The composition ω ↦ φ(X ω) is μ-integrable: it is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ and has finite integral.
conclusions: φ(∫ ω, X ω ∂μ) ≤ ∫ ω, φ(X ω) ∂μ, where both integrals are Bochner integrals of ℝ-valued functions against μ and ≤ is the standard order on ℝ.
Equivalently, in probabilistic notation: φ(E[X]) ≤ E[φ(X)] — Jensen's inequality for a convex φ : ℝ → ℝ and an integrable real random variable X on a probability space.
mathematical_definitions: Expectation / integral (LocalDef001): for a measure μ on a measurable space Ω and X : Ω → ℝ, LocalDef001 μ X := ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ, the Bochner integral; since μ is a probability measure this is the expectation E[X]. The Bochner integral yields the junk value 0 for non-integrable functions.
ConvexOn ℝ s f: the set s is convex and f(a•x + b•y) ≤ a•f(x) + b•f(y) for all x, y ∈ s and all scalars a, b ≥ 0 with a + b = 1. Here s = Set.univ = ℝ and the scalar action is real multiplication.
Integrable f μ: MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f μ ∧ MeasureTheory.HasFiniteIntegral f μ (i.e. ∫⁻ ‖f ω‖₊ dμ < ∞).
Set.univ : Set ℝ is {x | True}, all of ℝ.
The norm on ℝ throughout is the absolute value, and the topology/uniformity is the standard one induced by d(x,y) = |x − y|.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let (Ω, 𝔉, μ) be a probability space and let X : Ω → ℝ be a random variable. Let φ : ℝ → ℝ be convex on all of ℝ. If X is μ-integrable and φ ∘ X is μ-integrable, then φ of the expectation of X is at most the expectation of φ(X): φ(∫ X dμ) ≤ ∫ φ(X) dμ. This is Jensen's inequality for real-valued random variables, stated with both integrability conditions assumed rather than derived, and with convexity assumed on the entire real line rather than on a smaller convex set containing the range of X.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Convexity is required on Set.univ = all of ℝ, not merely on an interval or convex set containing the essential range of X. This makes the hypothesis strictly stronger than the sharpest form of Jensen's inequality (which needs convexity only on a convex set where X lives a.e.), so the statement does not cover e.g. φ(x) = -log x or φ(x) = x log x, which are convex only on (0, ∞).

Integrability of the composition φ ∘ X is assumed rather than deduced. In the classical statement for convex φ on ℝ the negative part of φ(X) is automatically integrable and E[φ(X)] may be +∞; here the finiteness of E[φ(X)] is an added hypothesis, which weakens the conclusion's scope (the +∞ case is excluded rather than proven).

The Bochner integral assigns the junk value 0 to non-integrable functions; the hypotheses hX and hφX rule out this degenerate reading, so the conclusion is about genuine expectations. Without them the statement would be about junk values.
No measurability assumption is placed on X beyond what Integrable supplies (a.e. strong measurability); X need not be measurable in the strict sense, only a.e. strongly measurable.

Vacuity risk is low but nonzero in the following sense: the hypothesis set is satisfiable (e.g. Ω a point, μ a Dirac measure, X and φ arbitrary continuous with φ convex), so the theorem is not vacuous. However the pair (hφ on all of ℝ, hφX) jointly restricts the applicable class of φ substantially.
The probability-measure instance is essential: for a general measure with μ(Ω) ≠ 1 the inequality is false (the statement does not encode any normalization other than through IsProbabilityMeasure).
Ω is universe-polymorphic and may be empty; but IsProbabilityMeasure μ forces μ(Ω) = 1 > 0, so Ω is nonempty and the degenerate empty-space case cannot arise.
The statement gives no equality/strictness information: it says nothing about when equality holds (e.g. strict convexity forcing X to be a.e. constant), nor any quantitative gap.
ambiguities: LocalDef001 is anonymized; its body unambiguously unfolds to MeasureTheory.integral μ X, but the intended notational role (expectation E[X] versus a general Bochner integral) must be inferred from the IsProbabilityMeasure instance rather than from the definition itself.

It cannot be determined from the dossier whether the source statement intended convexity on the whole line or on a smaller convex set; the Lean statement commits to Set.univ, and whether that is a faithful rendering or a strengthening of the source hypothesis cannot be judged blind.
Likewise, whether the source theorem assumed integrability of φ ∘ X or derived/allowed E[φ(X)] = +∞ cannot be determined from the dossier alone.
